misconceptions.believed: That requiring two of three signals was a sufficient guard against handing out labels cheaply. Two thresholds cleared is not a coincidence and one is, which was the whole reasoning behind the number.
misconceptions.revealed_by: test_an_empty_codebase_has_no_class, written as an afterthought while listing the ways a class system goes wrong. It failed immediately: VibeVector() classified as a Loopwright.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Loopwright's signals are 'comprehensions in at most 15%' and 'generator expressions in at most 10%', and an empty codebase satisfies both by having no code. A class now needs at least one positive signal as well as its two: absence can corroborate a reading -- a real Loopwright genuinely does avoid comprehensions -- but it can never establish one.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: The rule counted evidence, and the failure was that absence is not evidence of the same kind. A threshold of the form 'at most X' is satisfied by the empty set, by the null hypothesis, by having never tried -- so any scoring system treating it as interchangeable with 'at least X' hands out its most confident answer to its least informative input. Same shape as M1, free points on an axis measuring nothing, arrived at from the opposite direction. Worth asking of any predicate: what does the empty case score?

decisions.decision: A class needs at least one positive signal, not merely two of any kind
alternatives: Two of three regardless of direction
decisions.rationale: M54. An at_most signal is satisfied by an empty codebase, so absence alone would earn the most confident label from the least informative input.

decisions.decision: derive_class takes a VibeVector and nothing else
alternatives: Pass the whole Session and read the vector from it
decisions.rationale: Exit criterion 6 becomes a property of the signature rather than a rule someone has to remember. Enforcement by argument list is the cheapest kind there is.

decisions.decision: Every class has exactly three signals
alternatives: Let each class have as many as its habit suggests
decisions.rationale: 'Cleared 3 of 3' has to mean the same thing across classes, or ranking by signals met silently favours whichever class was given the fewest.

decisions.decision: Equally good fits are printed beside the winner
decisions.rationale: Three classes clear every signal on this repository and the winner is decided by margin. Hiding that presents a coin toss as a reading, which is the horoscope the hazard names.

decisions.decision: A codebase that does not lean gets None
alternatives: A default class such as Generalist
decisions.rationale: A default class is a label nobody earned. 'Your code does not lean hard enough in any one direction to name' is a description rather than a gap.

decisions.decision: Classes live in profiler.py, not with mastery
decisions.rationale: It reads the Vibe Vector and belongs with style_signature and derive_tags, which do the same. Keeping it out of the mastery module means the two layers cannot be blended by accident.

Three classes tie at 3/3 on this repository and the tie-break is margin. Margin is a defensible ordering and it is still an ordering over things the design says are not ordered. Should a tie be shown as a genuine tie -- 'you are equally a Comprehensionist and an Architect' -- rather than resolved?

The class is derived on demand and never stored. That is what keeps criterion 6 trivially true, but it also means a player cannot see that their class changed when they re-profiled, which is the most interesting thing a class could ever tell them. Worth storing a history?
